record.original_question: Within the class of tiling billiards in periodic tilings, is there a finite list of generic archetypal behaviors? In particular, does a general dichotomy hold in which typical trajectories are either dense in open sets or integrable in the sense of being periodic or linearly escaping?

evidence.quote: Two questions In the following, I ask two questions, related in spirit – one general and one specific. Question 1.In the class of tiling billiards in periodic tilings, is there a finite list of generic archetypal behaviors? For instance, the tiling billiards for which generic behavior is under- stood fall into one of two categories: either their typical trajectories are dense in open sets of the plane, as in cases 1. and 5., or the behavior is integrable (typical trajectories are either periodic or linearly escaping), as in cases 2. and 3. (and conjecturally in case 4. as well). One could ask whether such a dichotomy holds in general.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A tiling billiard is a dynamical system defined as follows. Fix a locally finite tiling $\mathcal{T}$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ by polygons (the "tiles"), and assume $\mathcal{T}$ is invariant under a rank-2 lattice of translations (a periodic tiling). A point particle moves along straight segments inside each tile; when it crosses an edge separating two adjacent tiles, its direction is updated by Snell's law of refraction with refraction coefficient $-1$, i.e. the outgoing trajectory is the reflection of the incoming trajectory across the crossed edge (rather than across the normal to that edge). A trajectory is called periodic if it closes up after finitely many edge crossings, drift-periodic if it is invariant under a non-trivial translation of the tiling, linearly escaping if its distance from its starting point grows asymptotically linearly in time without being drift-periodic, and dense in an open set $U \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ if its closure contains $U$.

(a) Does there exist a finite list of "archetypal" behaviors such that, for every periodic tiling $\mathcal{T}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$, the typical (in the sense of Lebesgue-almost-every initial condition in phase space) trajectory of the associated tiling billiard exhibits one of the behaviors on this list?

(b) More specifically, does the following dichotomy hold for every periodic tiling $\mathcal{T}$: for Lebesgue-almost every initial condition, the trajectory is either
  (i) dense in some open subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$, or
  (ii) integrable, in the sense of being periodic or linearly escaping?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in surveys of tiling billiards. Recent research (e.g., results on triangle tiling billiards and the Rauzy gasket, the trihexagonal tiling, brick tilings, and deviations for generalized tiling billiards in cyclic polygons) has confirmed the proposed dichotomy in additional specific families of tilings, but no general classification or proof of the dichotomy across all periodic tilings has been established.

status_evidence.title: Triangle tiling billiards and the exceptional family of their escaping trajectories
status_evidence.snippet: Studies triangle tiling billiards, proving that almost all trajectories are either closed or escape linearly; the exceptional escaping family is linked to the Rauzy gasket.
status_evidence.claim: The integrable side of the dichotomy is established for triangle tiling billiards but not in general.

status_evidence.title: Periodicity and ergodicity in the trihexagonal tiling
status_evidence.snippet: Generic trajectories in the trihexagonal tiling billiard are dense in open subsets of the plane.
status_evidence.claim: The 'dense in open sets' side of the dichotomy is established in the trihexagonal case.

status_evidence.title: Deviations for generalized tiling billiards in cyclic polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work extends the analysis to generalized tiling billiards in cyclic polygons, indicating the general classification problem remains active.
status_evidence.claim: The classification problem is still being actively investigated and is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: General Behavior of Brick Tiling Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Thesis analyzing brick tiling billiards as a further specific case of the conjectured archetypal behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Additional specific tilings have been studied since the question was posed, supporting but not proving the general dichotomy.
